questions.stem: According to the passage, in what year did Martin Luther King Jr. deliver the "I Have a Dream" speech?
questions.evidence: One of the most famous events related to him came in 1963.
questions.explanation_ko: 나에게는 꿈이 있습니다 연설과 관련된 유명한 사건은 1963년에 있었다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT something the Civil Rights Act of 1964 did?
options: Ended the legal separation of people by race in public places
Banned job discrimination based on race
Guaranteed equal voting rights for all Americans
Banned job discrimination based on religion
questions.evidence: The Civil Rights Act was important, but it did not address all kinds of racial discrimination. For example, black Americans still did not have the same voting rights as white Americans
questions.explanation_ko: 1964년 민권법은 공공장소 인종 분리 종식과 고용 차별 금지는 이루었지만, 투표권 평등까지 보장하지는 않았다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the fact that King urged peaceful action after police attacked protesters in Alabama, and this pushed Congress to pass the Voting Rights Act?
options: The violent police attack in Alabama had no effect on national politics.
The nonviolent response to the attack in Alabama helped build the pressure that led Congress to pass the Voting Rights Act.
King approved of using violence in response to the police attack.
The Voting Rights Act was passed before the events in Alabama.
questions.evidence: The events in Alabama pushed Congress to pass the Voting Rights Act.
questions.explanation_ko: 앨라배마 사건이 의회가 투표권법을 통과시키도록 압박했다는 내용에서, 비폭력 대응이 그 법 통과에 힘을 실었음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that King was assisting a workers' strike in Tennessee when he was killed?
options: To show that King's activism had expanded to economic equality issues shortly before his death
To explain why King moved to Tennessee permanently
To argue that workers' strikes are dangerous
To describe King's early career as a labor organizer
questions.evidence: In the following years, King worked for economic equality. In April 1968, he was attending a workers’ strike in Tennessee.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 설명은 킹이 사망 직전 경제적 평등을 위한 활동으로 관심을 넓혔음을 보여 주기 위한 것입니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "discrimination" mean in "banned job discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion or national origin"?
options: unfair treatment based on a group a person belongs to
questions.evidence: The act also banned job discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion or national origin
questions.explanation_ko: discrimination은 소속 집단을 이유로 한 불공정한 대우를 뜻합니다.

key_points: Martin Luther King Jr. led the nonviolent civil rights movement in the 1960s and delivered his famous 'I Have a Dream' speech during the 1963 March on Washington.
His activism helped pass the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which ended legal racial segregation in public places and banned job discrimination, though it did not secure equal voting rights.
After police attacked voting-rights protesters in Alabama in 1965, King urged nonviolence, and the events helped lead to the Voting Rights Act, signed that August.
King, who later focused on economic equality, was assassinated in April 1968 while supporting a workers' strike in Tennessee; the U.S. began observing Martin Luther King Day in 1986.
main_idea: Martin Luther King Jr. led the nonviolent U.S. civil rights movement, helping secure major legislation like the Civil Rights Act and Voting Rights Act, before being assassinated in 1968 while advocating for economic equality.
restate_sentence: King is remembered for his non-violent protests against the unequal treatment of African-Americans.
